items.title: Cache the last forecast so the app opens offline
items.note: BUILT — needs a device test on a real flight-mode phone
items.detail:
Click any item to open this side panel. Details accept HTML, so an agent can leave a structured hand-off here.

Plan (written by the agent):

  • Store the last successful response in app storage with its timestamp.
  • On launch, render the cached forecast immediately and refresh in the background.
  • Show a small “as of 14:05” label when the data is older than an hour.

This item was edited by the agent in its last session, which is why it is ringed in amber when ✨ last update is on.

notes.title: How this roadmap works (read me first)
notes.html:
Releases hold items. Items you have not committed to live in the Backlog. Free-form notes like this one sit at the bottom.

Click an item to read its details in the side panel · ✎ to edit · ⠿ to drag · checkbox to select rows · ＋ Release to add a release · ▲▼ on a release header to reorder releases.

Numbers and bulk actions. Every row is numbered 1..n inside its release, so you and your agent can both say “item 3”. Tick a few rows and the release header becomes a bar that marks them done, moves them to another release or deletes them — and a ticked set drags as one block.

Saving. Right now this demo lives in your browser only. Press 💾 Save (or Create new file… in the banner) to write a roadmap-data.json next to your project. From then on the page autosaves to that file and watches it for changes — the green dot means it is live.

Export / Import give you a plain JSON copy at any time. Trash keeps everything you delete until you empty it.

notes.title: Working with an AI coding agent
notes.html:
The point of this tool: you and your agent edit the same file. You use this page; the agent uses roadmap.py from the terminal (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Copilot — anything that can run a Python script).

Every node the agent touches is stamped, so the ✨ last update toggle in the header rings exactly what changed in its most recent session — NEW, EDITED, MOVED, or a struck-through ghost row for deletions. Turn it on now: two items in v1.1 and one deleted item were touched by a demo agent session. Use ‹ older / newer › to walk back through earlier sessions.

If you both edit the same field before the file syncs, your edit wins and the agent's version is listed in a red banner so nothing is lost silently.

Tell your agent about the tool by pasting the snippet from agent-instructions.md into your CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md or rules file.
